name: --port
default: os.environ.get('ARM_SERIAL_PORT') or ('COM6' if os.name == 'nt' else None)
meaning: Mega serial port (env ARM_SERIAL_PORT); default = auto-detect

name: --awake
meaning: the arm is NOT on the cradle, whatever rest_state.json says (it was moved off by hand)

name: --rest-file
meaning: f"where the arm's rest state is remembered (default {REST_FILE}; '' = no memory; always off with --port SIMULATED)"

name: --resting
meaning: the arm is on the cradle (autoen was restarted while it rested): Start moves nothing and waits, paused, for the wake task (POST /api/task {"kind": "wake"}), then Resume

name: --pose-config
meaning: extra poses + rest/wake sequences (default PRISM/config/poses.json; '' = no rest pose)

name: --poses
meaning: optional poses file (so101_dpad_poses.json: up/right/left/down); default = the built-in poses of arm_node.py

name: --grip-cal
meaning: gripper calibration from grip_calibrate.py: its open / fast-close / block-window values become the defaults (options given here still win). '' = ignore it

name: --mqtt-host
meaning: broker (env MQTT_HOST)

name: --mqtt-hz
meaning: arm/telemetry rate

name: --no-mqtt
meaning: run without a broker (the recording and the page still work)

name: --web-host
meaning: address of the page; 0.0.0.0 exposes a page that can MOVE THE ROBOT to your network

name: --cycles-per-set
meaning: default 2 sets x 6 = one magazine of 12 blocks

name: --rpm
meaning: belt speed to the IR, real output-shaft rpm (CPR 11880; the old '60' at CPR 1320 = 6.7)

name: --arm-speed
meaning: 1.0 = the project's normal pose speed

name: --gap
meaning: pause between cycles, s

name: --hz
meaning: samples per second

name: --first-drop
meaning: side of the first drop when alternating

name: --carry-speed
meaning: speed factor after the grip (Home and drop legs)

name: --acc
meaning: servo acceleration 0-254 (x100 ticks/s2), sent as the 4th field of P; 8 = the firmware default; only the ACC firmware reads it

name: --open-pos
meaning: gripper open ticks (default: see --grip-open-pos-a / pose 'up')

name: --enable-a
meaning: feature A: fast pre-close P move + a lower default gripper-open position. 0 = exact original behaviour (open_pos from pose 'up', single-speed stall-crawl all the way)

name: --grip-open-pos-a
meaning: feature A: --open-pos default used when --open-pos is not given and --enable-a=1 (~215 deg, was ~249 deg from pose 'up'). UNVERIFIED on real blocks -- confirm the gripper still clears a block at this opening before trusting it

name: --grip-fast-to-pos
meaning: feature A: fast P-move target before the stall-crawl takes over, ticks (~200 deg). Must stay ABOVE the real block height (open_pos is in ticks too; smaller ticks = more closed) or the fast move has no stall protection and can hit the block hard. UNVERIFIED --

name: --grip-pos
meaning: close the gripper to exactly this J6 position (ticks, taught on a real block with grip_calibrate.py) and stop there, instead of the firmware stall-crawl that closes until the jaws cannot move (that crunched blocks). 0 = stall-crawl

name: --grip-pos-speed
meaning: ticks/s of the last move to --grip-pos

name: --grip-fast-speed
meaning: feature A: speed of the fast pre-close P move, ticks/s (max 3200). ROUND 1 FINDING: a short one-shot P move is acceleration-bound, not speed-bound, so raising this alone does nothing -- see --grip-fast-acc

name: --grip-fast-acc
meaning: feature A: servo acceleration (0-254, x100 ticks/s^2) for JUST the fast pre-close move; every other move still uses --acc. ROUND 1 measured the default --acc (8) making a 170-tick fast move take 0.86s (acceleration-bound: t=2*sqrt(distance/acc)); ROUND 2 confi

name: --grip-fast-timeout
meaning: feature A: seconds allowed for the fast pre-close move before giving up and letting the stall-crawl cover the remaining distance

name: --enable-b
meaning: feature B: overlap the next block's FEED+belt-travel with this block's CARRY/RELEASE/HOME instead of doing them fully serially (TRANSPORT is ~46%% of the baseline cycle, almost all of it the arm standing still). See one_cycle_pipelined()'s docstring for the fu

name: --enable-d
meaning: feature D: send a configurable hold preload/torque-limit with C,6 instead of the firmware's fixed 150-tick, no-torque-cap default. 0 = exact original behaviour

name: --grip-hold-preload
meaning: feature D: extra ticks the firmware squeezes past the measured contact point while carrying (firmware default: fixed at 150, so 150 here reproduces it). ROUND 1 FINDING: lowering this to 60 did NOT reduce J6's CARRY current (748-812 mA either way -- the STS321

name: --grip-hold-torque-limit
meaning: feature D: STS3215 torque limit (0-1000 = 0-100%%) applied only while holding the block after G,CLOSED. 1000 = off/no cap. ROUND 1 ran with this off and lowered --grip-hold-preload instead, which did not reduce current. ROUND 2's writeWord() call was not retri

name: --enable-verify
meaning: 1 = a grip that stops outside the block window is GRIP_MISS (retried), a GRIP must start with a block at the IR, and a carry with a weak/slipping J6 is logged GRIP_SUSPECT instead of OK. 0 = old behaviour

name: --grip-contact-min-deg
meaning: G,CLOSED position window that means 'a block is held' (clean grips measured 181.8-182.0 deg, air grips 165-172). Widen it if blocks vary; UNVERIFIED beyond the 6 clean grips of the 200956 run

name: --grip-contact-max-deg
meaning: upper end of the block window, deg

name: --grip-carry-min-ma
meaning: J6 current peak while carrying below this = GRIP_SUSPECT. 0 = off (default): it flagged almost every clean carry as soon as the hold torque limit went under ~150 (peaks were 6-13 mA at 50, 32 mA at 100, 110-150 mA at 180); the contact-angle window is the relia

name: --grip-slip-max-deg
meaning: J6 moving more than this while carrying = GRIP_SUSPECT (clean carries moved <= 0.26 deg)

name: --enable-recover
meaning: pipelined mode only: after a failed cycle open the gripper, go Home then Standby and bring a block to the IR (belt first, feeder only if the belt is empty) before the next cycle; a recovery that fails stops the run

name: --enable-f
meaning: feature F (flow): the optimizer plans every feed (POST /api/feed), the belt brings blocks while the arm works, a pick never waits for a cycle end. Overrides B / C.

name: --enable-c
meaning: feature C, belt queue (needs --enable-b): after one unqueued cycle has measured the full belt travel time, a 2nd block is dropped on the moving belt --queue-split of the way through, so afterwards every CONV only moves the next block about HALF the belt (short

name: --pause-before-set
meaning: 1 = pause before every set (also the first) until Resume / experiment.py resumes it; while paused, POST /api/task can run a belt test or baseline. 0 = off (default, unchanged behaviour)

name: --queue-split
meaning: where on the lead block's trip the 2nd block is dropped, as a fraction of the full travel time (0.5 = the two end up half a belt apart)

name: --arrival-guard
meaning: 1 = (pipeline) hold X,CONV back so the next block cannot reach the IR before the arm is parked at Standby (+ --arrival-margin-s); estimated from the last 3 cycles. 0 = start CONV at the gate as before

name: --arrival-margin-s
meaning: how long after the arm is parked the block may arrive at the earliest

name: --ir-confirm-s
meaning: how long GRIP waits for the IR telemetry to show the block (it streams ~10 Hz, so the reading right after ARRIVED can be stale) before it calls the IR empty (NO_BLOCK_AT_IR)

name: --recover-conv-s
meaning: seconds the recovery runs the belt looking for a block already on it before it feeds a new one (the full feed->IR run is ~5 s at 33 rpm)

name: --move-timeout
meaning: seconds allowed per arm move

name: --feed-timeout
meaning: seconds to wait for FEED_DONE

name: --arrive-timeout
meaning: seconds for a block to reach the IR

name: --clear-timeout
meaning: seconds for the block to leave the IR after the pick

name: --grip-timeout
meaning: seconds to wait for G,CLOSED / G,ERROR

name: --offset
meaning: extra encoder counts the belt travels after the IR triggers

name: --temp-max
meaning: belt motor over-temperature trip, C (0 = off)

name: --belt-wdt-ms
meaning: belt watchdog timeout sent via X,WDT (0 = off, not recommended). Default: 500 (firmware default, unchanged) when --enable-b=0; 1500 when --enable-b=1 -- feature B measured FAULT_1 (watchdog) in 2/10 pipelined cycles at the firmware default even though the PC k

name: --kp
meaning: belt speed PID, PWM per rpm of error. 9 x the firmware default 0.5 / 1.5 / 0, which was tuned with CPR 1320: at CPR 11880 the same belt speed reads 9x fewer rpm, so x9 gives the same PWM

name: --feeder-ready
meaning: ready angle the blade waits at before the push (= home: no visible first move)

name: --feeder-ready-ms
meaning: wait at the ready angle (0 = no ready stop)

name: --feeder-ramp-ms
meaning: slow sweep ready -> push angle (0 = jump)

name: --max-fails
meaning: stop after this many failed cycles in a row

name: --hold-tol
meaning: while the arm should stand still, a joint further than this (ticks) from its pose is logged and pulled back; 0 = off

name: --settle-tol
meaning: a joint that stops this close (ticks) outside the pose window for 1.5 s counts as arrived; 0 = off

name: --cpr
meaning: belt encoder counts per output revolution: 11 PPR x 4 (quadrature) x 1:270 (JGB37-520, 37 rpm). Sent to the Mega as X,CPR at Start; it sets what every belt rpm means

name: --web-port
meaning: 0 = no web page

name: --open-page
meaning: open this page in the browser at start (default: no - the PRISM dashboard :8080 is the page; this address stays on because the optimizer and the dashboard send their commands to it)

name: --auto-start
meaning: start the run immediately (default: open the web page and wait for the Start button)

name: --yes
meaning: with --auto-start: skip the 'arm area is clear' question

name: --shadow
meaning: compute and log plans, send nothing to autoen

name: --objective
meaning: efficiency (default) = safety always, then 1 good cubes per minute, 2 energy; priority = 1 safety, 2 energy, 3 speed; or throughput / energy / balanced

name: --keep-budget
meaning: leave autoen's sets / cycles per set as they were started (default: the optimizer owns the run and raises them, so it never 'finishes' in the middle of the work)

name: --no-frontier
meaning: stay inside the tested grid (default: try one step at a time beyond what it has proven)

name: --lam
meaning: balanced: J per second of cycle time

name: --j-limit
meaning: only configs with at most this many J per cube

name: --probe-s
meaning: IDLE: resume to try a feed after this many seconds

name: --auto-resume
meaning: IDLE: probe the feeder when forecast.py expects a refill (history in forecast_state.json)

name: --no-sort
meaning: do not sort by colour (autoen keeps its own drop order)

name: --no-auto-recover
meaning: every abnormal cycle -> ALERT, wait for a person (default: answer it itself, incidents.py)

name: --no-stuck-alert
meaning: a cube still on the running belt is only logged (default: brake + ALERT)

name: --no-brake
meaning: IDLE: leave the belt coasting (the brake saves ~0.05 W)

name: --max-s
meaning: stop after this many seconds (tests)

name: --colors
meaning: comma-separated colours to detect, in priority order, e.g. white,red,blue (default: the 'enabled' list of vision_calibration.json, else white)

name: --list-colors
meaning: print the available colours and exit

name: --belt-axis
meaning: image axis along the belt (u = x, v = y). Default: from calibration, else u

name: --belt-dir
meaning: +1 if that coordinate GROWS in the direction of travel, -1 if it shrinks

name: --calibrate
meaning: open the calibration window (ROI, count line, colours, belt direction) and exit

name: --no-roi
meaning: run WITHOUT a conveyor ROI (old behaviour: the colours are counted anywhere in the frame)

name: --show
meaning: ALSO open the camera window on the Pi's desktop (default: none - the picture is on the dashboard; a window costs RAM and CPU for nothing)

name: --no-background
meaning: do NOT learn the empty belt (old behaviour: a reflection on the belt can count as white)
